title: Tuning by search
summary: Let the Analyze ▸ Optimize tab tune an LQR balancer: fastest recovery within a motor's force budget, and what happens when the goal leaves something out.

steps.title: Fast costs force
steps.text:
The LQR balancer recovers from a 5° tilt in under a second, but it pushes with up to 6.8 N. Suppose the motor can only give 5 N without overheating.

The weight r prices the force: raise it and the controller pushes more gently, but recovers more slowly. Run the default to see the starting point.

check.hint: Load the setup and press Run.
check.success: 0.89 s with 6.8 N. Now find the fastest recovery that stays within 5 N.

steps.title: Search for r
steps.text:
You could try values of r by hand. The Analyze ▸ Optimize tab does it for you: it is set to vary r between 0.01 and 10 and minimize the settling time, keeping Max |F| at or below 5 N.

Press Optimize. Each point on its plot is one simulation.

check.hint: Press Optimize in the Analyze ▸ Optimize tab and let it finish.
check.success: r ≈ 0.29: 1.05 s using 4.93 N. The best point sits right on the force limit: faster recovery always takes more force, so the search pushes r down until the limit stops it.

steps.title: Two knobs
steps.text:
Now let the search vary two weights: qx, how much the controller cares about the cart's position, and r. Same goal, same 5 N limit.

Press Optimize. Does it beat 1.05 s?

check.hint: Press Optimize and wait for it to finish (about 60 runs).
check.success: About 0.47 s, and with only 2.4 N! The search drove qx to the bottom of its range. That looks too good: what did it give up?

steps.title: Watch the cart
steps.text: Press "Apply best inputs" in the Analyze ▸ Optimize tab, then run. Watch the cart in the Angle and position tab, and read the Largest cart excursion in the Summary (0.15 m with r ≈ 0.29 alone, 0.13 m at the defaults).

check.hint: Use the best inputs (qx ≈ 0.1, r ≈ 2.5) and run.
check.success: The cart wanders about 0.45 m, three times as far, and is still 0.16 m off target after 8 s.

steps.title: You get what you ask for
steps.text: Why did the search make qx so small?

options: The settling time only watches the angle, so caring less about the cart freed the controller to straighten the pole
A small qx makes the pole lighter, so it is easier to balance
The search went wrong; with more runs it would raise qx
check.hint: Which quantity was the search told to make small, and what does it measure?
check.success: An optimizer finds the best answer to the question you asked, loopholes included. To keep the cart home, put it in the question: a limit on Largest cart excursion, or a goal that includes it.
